message.content:
Renting an apartment in New York City varies widely depending on the borough, neighborhood, size, and building amenities. As a rough guide:

| Neighborhood / Borough | Typical 1‑bedroom rent (mid‑2024) |
|------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| Manhattan (Upper East Side, Midtown, Chelsea) | $3,200 – $4,800 per month |
| Brooklyn (Williamsburg, Brooklyn Heights, Park Slope) | $2,800 – $4,200 per month |
| Queens (Long Island City, Astoria, Forest Hills) | $2,200 – $3,500 per month |
| Bronx (Riverdale, Pelham Bay) | $1,800 – $2,800 per month |
| Staten Island (St. George, Tompkinsville) | $1,600 – $2,400 per month |

These figures are averages; actual rents can be higher or lower based on exact location, building age, floor level, view, and included utilities. For a more precise estimate, you could look at current listings on real‑estate sites or contact local property managers.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What's the cost of renting an apartment in New York?" They want the cost of renting an apartment in New York. We have a tool to calculate construction cost, but not rental cost. There's no tool for rental cost. So we cannot use a tool. We need to answer with a best estimate. We can provide a general estimate. We should not mention the tool.
